questions.prompt: One system (e.g. Amazon) can combine several architectural patterns.
questions.explanation: Amazon uses microservices (pricing, inventory, shipping) AND event-driven flows (Order Placed → email).
questions.source: Week 4 Lecture 1 · 'One system can have one or many patterns'

questions.prompt: Group 1 (Stack Overflow): which MVC part covers business logic AND data access?
questions.explanation: Controller + View = presentation layer; Model = business logic + data access layers.
questions.source: Group 1 presentation · 'Where MVC fits inside the N-Layers'

questions.prompt: Stack Overflow runs Redis as a separate tier. What is it used for?
questions.explanation: Redis = distributed cache; Elasticsearch = full-text search; SQL Server = data tier.

questions.prompt: Group 2 (audio workstation): Noise Reduction → EQ → Reverb plug-ins act as…
questions.explanation: Microkernel loads the plug-ins; each plug-in is a filter, connected by pipes.

questions.prompt: Group 3: which pattern answers 'Who needs to know that this happened?'
questions.explanation: Broker: who should handle this request? Event Bus: who needs to know? Controller-Worker: how to divide the work?
questions.source: Group 3 presentation · 'How can these patterns work together?'

questions.prompt: Group 3: which tool does Uber use as its core message bus?
questions.explanation: Uber uses Apache Kafka as a core message bus for rider and driver event data.
questions.source: Group 3 presentation · 'Best real-world use case: Uber'

questions.prompt: Group 4: why combine an Interpreter with a Blackboard?
options: Experts can change rules without recompiling
It makes the system run faster
questions.explanation: The interpreter reads human-written rules on the fly, so non-programmers can change behaviour without recompiling.

questions.prompt: Netflix group: a central component that controls the order of service calls is…
questions.explanation: Orchestration: a central component coordinates services and controls the order of operations.

questions.prompt: Group 7: Basecamp is a well-known example of…
questions.explanation: Basecamp ('The Majestic Monolith') is one Ruby on Rails (MVC) application deployed as a single unit.

questions.prompt: Which classic problem do containers solve?
options: 'It works on my machine…' but not on others
questions.explanation: A container packages code + dependencies, so it runs the same everywhere.
questions.source: Week 5 Lecture · 'It was working on my machine…'

questions.prompt: Which chain is correct?
questions.explanation: docker build turns a Dockerfile into an image; docker run turns an image into a container.

questions.prompt: Cookie analogy: the Docker IMAGE is the ___, the CONTAINER is the ___
questions.explanation: Image = recipe (blueprint). Container = cookie made from it - one recipe, many cookies.
questions.source: Week 5 Lecture · 'What is a Docker image?'

questions.prompt: Containers vs virtual machines - containers…
questions.explanation: A VM copies a whole OS; containers isolate at the process level and share the host kernel.

questions.prompt: Which port does the app listen on inside the container?
questions.explanation: -p HostPort:ContainerPort → 80 on your machine, 8080 inside the container.

questions.prompt: A server that stores and distributes Docker images is called a…
questions.explanation: Registry (e.g. Docker Hub) = where images live when they are not on your machine.

questions.prompt: You run `docker run` but the image doesn't exist locally. What does Docker do?
questions.explanation: Engine process: 1) check local image, 2) if not found, pull from Docker Hub, 3) create container…

questions.prompt: Group 1: in Stack Overflow's design, which layer is NOT covered by MVC?
questions.explanation: Controller+View = presentation; Model = business + data access; database layer is outside MVC.
questions.source: Group 1 presentation · 'Where MVC fits inside the N-Layers'

questions.prompt: Group 3: a big risk of the broker architecture is…
options: The broker is a single point of failure
questions.explanation: If the central broker fails, communication stops (unless high-availability clustering is used).

questions.prompt: Group 7: why does Basecamp stay monolithic?
options: Simpler development and operations for the team
questions.explanation: One app and one database keep development simple; microservices would add complexity without a clear need.

questions.prompt: Containers isolate applications at the ___ level, VMs at the OS level.
questions.explanation: Containers isolate at the process level and share the host kernel.

questions.prompt: When Docker starts a container, what do cgroups do?
options: Limit resources such as CPU and memory
Map host ports to container ports
questions.explanation: Namespaces isolate what a container can SEE; cgroups limit what it can USE.
questions.source: Week 5 Lecture · 'Docker run' / Docker Practice Session 1

questions.prompt: What does `--rm` do here?
options: Removes the container after it exits
questions.explanation: --rm cleans up the container automatically when it stops. (docker rmi removes images.)

questions.prompt: What does the Docker Engine do after `docker run`? Put the steps in order.
items: Check if the image exists locally
Pull it from Docker Hub if missing
Create the container from the image
questions.explanation: Image first (local, else pull), then create and isolate the container, limit it, wire the ports and start the process.

questions.prompt: Group 1 (Stack Overflow): put the steps of an upvote click in order.
items: View shows the new vote count
questions.explanation: Presentation (Controller) → Business logic (Model) → Data access (Model) → Database → back up to the View.

questions.prompt: Map port 3000 on your laptop to port 80 inside the container. What goes after `-p`?
questions.explanation: The rule is HostPort:ContainerPort, so 3000:80.
